title: Data dictionary + citation/usage guide for consumers
context: With the explorer and exports live, downstream consumers — genealogists, historians, educators, data scientists — need clear documentation of what each field means, how to cite the corpus in their own work, how to correctly interpret the provenance and evidence-rationale fields, and what the license terms allow. Without a data dictionary and usage guide, consumers may misuse or miscite the data, undermining the corpus's value and credibility.
objective: Write a data dictionary covering every entity type and field in the GEDCOM X-aligned corpus, and a citation/usage guide explaining how consumers should cite the corpus, how to interpret provenance and evidence-rationale fields, what the license terms permit, and how to report errors or request takedowns.
acceptanceCriteria: Data dictionary covers all entity types (Person, Name, Fact, Relationship, PlaceReference, SourceDescription, Evidence/Conclusion) with field names, data types, cardinality, and plain-language descriptions.
Each field's provenance and evidence-rationale slots explained with a worked example showing how to read a real assertion.
Citation guide provides: recommended citation format for the corpus as a whole, for individual persons, and for specific assertions; includes version, license, and access date fields.
Usage guide states what the CC0-1.0 (and any CC BY-SA / CC BY / ODbL) license permits and requires, including attribution obligations where applicable.
Error-reporting and takedown-request instructions included with a link to the report mechanism.
Documented in docs/data-dictionary.md and docs/usage-guide.md, committed via PR, with links from the explorer's landing page.
output: docs/data-dictionary.md and docs/usage-guide.md — data dictionary and citation/usage guide for corpus consumers, committed via PR.
